name: brew install
description: Install a formula or cask.

flags.description: Treat the name as a cask (GUI app)
Treat the name as a formula
Show what would be installed without installing
Install the development version from the HEAD branch
Compile from source instead of using a bottle

notes: Homebrew auto-updates before install; set HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 to skip
Install and upgrade show a summary and ask for confirmation by default (ask mode); pass -y or set HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1 for non-interactive use
Installing an already-installed but outdated formula upgrades it unless HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_UPGRADE is set

name: brew install --cask
description: Install a macOS application distributed as a cask.

examples.description: Upgrade casks including those that auto-update

notes: Casks that update themselves are skipped by brew upgrade unless --greedy is passed
The --no-quarantine flag is deprecated (Homebrew 5.0); casks that fail macOS Gatekeeper checks are being disabled in homebrew/cask

name: brew uninstall
description: Uninstall a formula or cask.

flags.description: Casks only: also remove app support files and preferences
Uninstall even if other formulae depend on it
Show what would be uninstalled and autoremoved

examples.description: Remove an app and all of its data

notes: Aliases: brew remove, brew rm
WARNING: --zap deletes user data and settings for the app (possibly shared with other apps) and cannot be undone

name: brew upgrade
description: Upgrade outdated formulae and casks.

flags.description: Also upgrade casks that auto-update or use version :latest
Only upgrade outdated formulae with known vulnerabilities (OSV.dev)

examples.description: Only upgrade formulae with high or critical vulnerabilities

notes: Pinned formulae and casks are skipped
brew update <formula> is now an alias for brew upgrade <formula>

name: brew update
description: Fetch the newest version of Homebrew and all formula/cask definitions.
notes: update does not upgrade installed packages; use brew upgrade for that
Alias: brew up. Passing a formula name (brew update <formula>) runs brew upgrade <formula> instead

name: brew outdated
description: List installed packages that have newer versions available.

flags.description: Only list outdated formulae with known vulnerabilities

name: brew pin
description: Prevent a formula or cask from being upgraded.

examples.description: Hold a cask at its current version

notes: Casks can be pinned since Homebrew 6.0, but casks that auto-update may still update themselves outside Homebrew
Packages that depend on newer versions of a pinned formula may not install or run correctly

name: brew search
description: Search formulae and casks by name or regex.

flags.description: Search descriptions as well as names

name: brew info
description: Show information about a formula or cask: versions, dependencies, caveats.

flags.description: Show the size of installed formulae and casks
Open the package's source on GitHub

examples.description: Show version, deps, and caveats for node
See how much space each installed package uses

notes: Re-read the Caveats section after installing: it often contains PATH or service instructions

name: brew list
description: List installed formulae and casks, or files of a given package.

examples.description: Show files installed by a formula

notes: Alias: brew ls

name: brew leaves
description: List installed formulae that are not dependencies of another installed formula.

flags.description: Only show those you installed explicitly

name: brew deps
description: Show the dependencies of a formula.

flags.description: Use the packages in ./Brewfile (or --brewfile=<path>) as input

examples.description: Review what a Brewfile will pull in before installing

name: brew uses
description: Show formulae and casks that depend on a given formula.
notes: Without --installed it lists every known formula and cask that depends on it

name: brew services list
description: List background services managed by Homebrew and their status.

name: brew services start
description: Start a service now and register it to start at login.

examples.description: Start Postgres and enable it on login
Start without registering to launch at login

notes: WARNING: sudo brew services registers a boot-time service that runs as root and trusts the Homebrew prefix owner; avoid unless needed
Persistent environment overrides go in ~/.homebrew/services/<formula>.env (KEY=value lines) and survive upgrades; apply with brew services restart

name: brew services stop
description: Stop a service and unregister it from starting at login.

name: brew tap
description: Add a third-party repository of formulae and casks.

examples.description: Install by full name (trusts just that formula)
Trust the whole tap so short names like 'brew install terraform' work

notes: Since Homebrew 6.0, non-official taps must be trusted (brew trust) before Homebrew will load their formulae, casks or commands
Only tap repositories you trust; formulae run arbitrary install code

name: brew untap
description: Remove a tapped repository.

flags.description: Uninstall all formulae and casks from the tap first

examples.description: Remove a tap (offers to uninstall its packages first)
Uninstall the tap's packages and remove it without asking

notes: WARNING: --force uninstalls every formula and cask installed from that tap

name: brew cleanup
description: Remove old versions and stale downloads from the cache.

flags.description: Remove cache files older than N days (all to remove everything)
Scrub the cache, including downloads for the latest versions

examples.description: Clean up old versions and cache

notes: install/upgrade/reinstall clean up the affected packages automatically, and everything every 30 days, unless HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP is set
Downloads older than 120 days are removed by default (HOMEBREW_CLEANUP_MAX_AGE_DAYS)

name: brew autoremove
description: Uninstall formulae that were only installed as dependencies and are no longer needed.

name: brew doctor
description: Check the system for potential problems with the Homebrew setup.

examples.description: List individual checks you can run by name

notes: Warnings are not always fatal; fix them if you are seeing install problems
Also warns about untrusted third-party taps (see brew trust)

name: brew config
description: Show Homebrew and system configuration useful for debugging.

examples.description: Print version, prefix, CPU, macOS, etc.
Print the install prefix (/opt/homebrew on Apple Silicon)
Print a formula's prefix, handy for build flags

name: brew link
description: Symlink a formula's files into the Homebrew prefix.

flags.description: Re-link a cask's binaries, manpages and completions (Homebrew 7.0+)

examples.command: brew unlink node && brew link --overwrite --force node@24
examples.description: Make keg-only node@24 the active node
Preview which files would be linked or overwritten

notes: Keg-only formulae (e.g. versioned ones) are not linked by default; brew info shows how to add them to PATH instead
Since Homebrew 5.1, a versioned keg-only formula is linked automatically when its unversioned sibling isn't installed

name: brew bundle dump
description: Write all installed formulae, casks, and taps to a Brewfile.

flags.description: Path of the Brewfile to write
Omit the package description comments (added by default)

examples.description: Add a formula to the Brewfile (--cask, --tap, --vscode, --go, --cargo, --npm... for other types)

notes: Brewfiles can also list Mac App Store apps, VS Code extensions, Go, Cargo, npm and uv packages, and more

name: brew bundle install
description: Install everything listed in a Brewfile.

flags.description: Do not upgrade already installed packages

examples.description: Set up a new Mac from dotfiles
Check whether all dependencies are installed and list what's missing
Uninstall anything not listed in the Brewfile (asks before removing)

notes: WARNING: brew bundle cleanup --force uninstalls every package not in the Brewfile without asking, and resets Homebrew's trust store to the Brewfile's entries

name: brew reinstall
description: Uninstall and reinstall a formula or cask with the same options.

flags.description: Treat names as casks or formulae
With --cask, remove all app files before reinstalling

examples.description: Reinstall a formula (e.g. after files were damaged)

name: brew trust
description: Allow Homebrew to load formulae, casks or commands from a non-official tap.

flags.description: Trust a single item instead of a whole tap

examples.description: Trust one formula so 'brew install terraform' works
Trust every current and future package in a tap
Revoke trust (brew untrust with no args lists untrusted items)

notes: Required since Homebrew 6.0: official taps are always trusted, third-party ones are not loaded until trusted
Prefer trusting individual items; trusting a tap lets all its Ruby code run with your user's privileges
Trust is stored in ~/.homebrew/trust.json (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/homebrew/trust.json)

name: brew vulns
description: Check installed formulae for known security vulnerabilities using OSV.dev.

flags.description: Only report findings at or above low, medium, high or critical
Also check dependencies of the named formulae
Only show vulnerabilities with a released fix
Check the formulae listed in a Brewfile

examples.description: High/critical issues you can fix by upgrading
Check specific formulae and their dependencies

notes: Built in since Homebrew 7.0; casks and formulae from untrusted taps are not scanned
A clean report does not guarantee there are no vulnerabilities

name: brew exec
description: Run a command from a formula without permanently adding it to your setup, like npx.

flags.description: Install these formulae if needed and put them on PATH for the command
Run inside Homebrew's sandbox, only allowing writes to <path>
Block network access inside the sandbox

examples.description: Run a tool, installing the formula that provides it if needed
Run a script with jq and yq on PATH

notes: Alias: brew x. Added in Homebrew 6.0
Formulae it needs are installed normally, so they remain installed afterwards

name: brew version-install
description: Install an older version of a formula by extracting it into a personal tap.

examples.description: Install a specific older version of jq as jq@1.7.1

notes: Added in Homebrew 5.1; the formula is extracted into the <user>/versions tap
Extracted old versions are not maintained or security-patched by Homebrew

name: brew shellenv
description: Print the shell commands that add Homebrew to PATH, MANPATH and INFOPATH.

examples.description: Add to ~/.zprofile on Apple Silicon Macs

notes: Pass the shell name explicitly (bash, zsh, fish, ...); auto-detection can guess wrong
